sources.title: On the non-vanishing of generalized Kato classes for elliptic curves of rank 2
sources.classified_claim: The paper explicitly replaces the analytic rank-two condition in its motivating question by an algebraic counterpart; Darmon-Rotger's equivalence including analytic rank two is stated as a conjecture, with rank=2 iff analytic order=2 identified as BSD rank two. Theorem A relates generalized-Kato nonvanishing to a strict Selmer condition, and Corollary B obtains nonvanishing only after assuming Mordell-Weil rank two and finite p-primary Sha.

sources.title: Shtukas and the Taylor expansion of L-functions
sources.classified_claim: For an unramified cuspidal PGL2 representation over a function field, the r-th central derivative of a quadratic base-change L-function is identified with the self-intersection of the corresponding Heegner-Drinfeld cycle.

sources.authors: David T.-B. G. Lilienfeldt; Ari Shnidman
sources.title: Derivatives of Rankin-Selberg L-functions and heights of generalized Heegner cycles
sources.classified_claim: A number-field central derivative of a Rankin-Selberg L-function is expressed by a Beilinson-Bloch height of a generalized Heegner cycle in higher weight. This is a first-central-derivative/higher-cycle result, not a second complex derivative rank-two theorem for E/Q.

sources.title: On the central derivatives of l-functions and modularity of heenger cycles
sources.classified_claim: The source gives an arithmetic intersection/global-height formula for a central L-derivative in higher weights. Its located statement concerns the derivative in the singular/first-derivative Gross-Zagier-Zhang direction, not an E/Q rank-two second-complex-derivative bridge.

sources.title: Integrals on p-adic upper half planes and Hida families over totally real fields
sources.classified_claim: Theorem 1.1 expresses a second derivative of a two-variable p-adic L-function along the Hida-family weight coordinate in terms of a squared p-adic logarithm of a global point. The second derivative is p-adic/family-directional, not the complex s-second derivative.
